chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
He was asked about a mouse that falls into a well, and it is not known about until after wudu (ablution) has been performed from it. Should the wudu be repeated? He said: “No.”

key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: the well from which the water was taken
key_terms.الْفَأْرَةِ: a mouse mentioned as the source of possible contamination
key_terms.الْوُضُوءُ: the ritual ablution whose repetition is being asked about
key_terms.لَا: the Imam’s negative answer, meaning it is not to be repeated
key_terms.يُتَوَضَّأُ: wudu (ablution) is performed using the water

ai.seo_question: If a mouse fell into a well and I only found out after performing wudu (ablution), must I repeat my wudu?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning wudu (ablution) performed with water from a well in which a mouse had fallen, when that was only discovered afterward. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام answers that the wudu does not need to be repeated, indicating the prior act remains valid in this case.
